messages.subject: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
messages.subject_clean: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
messages.body_plain:
I've ran into a problem installing R packages from private repositories on github. "github" source requires a password, which I don't want committed in the source code (that's a huge security hole). The closest I got to was to use a submodule and use local install. However, the lockfile contains the full path to the the source location which isn't very portable:

SourcePath:
  /Users/syrnick/xxxxx/vendor/rlibs/xyz-utils

It then fails to find the source of the package upon restore.

I also have to explicitly pass the location of the source explicitly to packrat::snapshot, but that's a minor nuisance. I just have a helper function that's goes over all private packages.

How do you deal with private repos?

Thanks!
Alex

messages.subject: Re: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
messages.subject_clean: How to manage dependency on private github repositories with packrat?
messages.body_plain: You're doing it the way we intended. The surprising thing is "it then fails to find the source of the package upon restore". When you're restoring, is there anything in ./packrat.sources/<packagename>? That's where packrat is supposed to go looking for it first, and we expect you to check the whole packrat.sources directory into source control.

messages.subject: Re: problem with tar
messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

Yes, this is generally a problem with R and Mavericks. By default R uses /usr/bin/gnutar on OS X, but gnutar was removed in Mavericks.

The safest workaround for now is to add the following to your .Renviron file:

TAR=/usr/bin/tar

We're considering an automatic workaround here (especially if R core doesn't fix this); this issue in Github has more information:

https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/37

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Re: Problem with bootstrap (decompress path)
messages.body_plain:
The most likely cause is that one of the source package paths isn't working correctly. Does it work if you supply an absolute path to the packages? (e.g. "pkg/" -> "~/myPkgs/pkg") This shouldn't be necessary, but if it is it might suggest where the problem is.

If your're still seeing this, the output of traceback() would be helpful.

Thanks for reporting this!

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Re: RStudio sees all packrat sources
messages.body_plain:
By default RStudio will index everything in your project directory, and that includes the contents of the library Packrat creates. I think the RStudio forum might be a better place for this question, but the best approach to making this smoother would probably involve a change on both ends--some mechanism to mark a directory as non-indexed for the RStudio project indexer, and a change to Packrat to use that mechanism.

Jonathan.

messages.subject: Status of packrat development
messages.body_plain:
Hi

I'd like to record package versions and their sources for the R projects I do. For this it seems that packrat is the ideal solution. I'm also co-maintaining the ProjectTemplate package, we were considering integrating packrat support so that it works "out of the box" for new projects.

Unfortunately, development of packrat seems to have stalled. Could you please comment -- does it just work "well enough", or has it turned out to be impractical in the long run? What are the future plans concerning this package, will it be on CRAN one day?

Best regards

Kirill

messages.subject: Re: Status of packrat development
messages.body_plain:
I'm a new user to packrat and it worked pretty well. I have a short wishlist (private git repo support, separating source storage from the repo), but that didn't stop us from rolling out packrat and we're happy with it.

Alex

messages.subject: Re: Status of packrat development
messages.body_plain:
There are certainly a few things we'd like to improve. And we do plan to get this on CRAN before too much time has passed; we've gotten some great input from the community in the last few months and that will help us prioritize what needs to get fixed before we release it more broadly.

We're hoping to start looking at community-supplied PRs in a couple of weeks (mid-March), and making some fixes of our own after that with an eye towards preparing for a CRAN submission.

Jonathan.
